self_assessment.note: Both positional survivors fail the natural-owner test, so ZERO of nine absence claims survive as sellable opportunities. Saturation findings are earned from the corpus; absence findings are not, and must be probed individually.

sampling_bias.issue: The corpus is DTC-challenger-only by construction — Agent -1 discovers advertisers by keyword search over ad copy, which surfaces brands buying heavily on direct response.
sampling_bias.consequence: It will systematically mistake incumbent-held positions for empty ones. dermatologist_as_ally is the worked example: challengers treat dermatologists adversarially, while Dove, CeraVe, Eucerin, SkinCeuticals and Bio-Oil all open on derm endorsement. The corpus saw only the challengers and read the position as vacant.

unclaimed_position_angles.description: Prevention for under-30s — selling before damage, to an audience the corpus only addresses after the fact.
unclaimed_position_angles.probe: in your 20s|before it starts|prevent(ion|ative) routine|early twenties|gen z

evidence: GoPure Skin Care uses the phrase mid-copy, opening instead on 'I used to think skincare stopped at my chin'. Term used as a qualifier, never as the opening.
Tiny field -- 16 ads in the whole category.

NOTE: a first probe, 'prevent wrinkles in your 20s', returned zero. That was an invented phrase and its zero was discarded rather than recorded -- it would have tested our vocabulary, not the category.

natural_owner_test.natural_owner: Good Molecules (and Biodance as a second check)
natural_owner_test.why: Good Molecules is the cheapest, most entry-level brand in the corpus — $6 eye cream, $12 serum — and price point is what makes a prevention pitch to younger buyers viable. Biodance is K-beauty/glass-skin with a young audience.
natural_owner_test.finding: Good Molecules runs 15 ads and opens on none of them with prevention; one opens on 'the best over 50 skincare', the opposite direction. Biodance runs 10 and opens on correction throughout — dry skin, tired under-eyes.
natural_owner_test.verdict: FAILS — both natural owners message correction, not prevention.

unclaimed_position_angles.description: Water quality — hard water and chlorine as the upstream cause. Adjacent categories run this hard; no skincare brand in the corpus touches it.

external_probe.query: hard water (+ eskiin ad set read directly)
evidence: 'hard water' returns only cleaning and appliance products. No skincare advertiser.

eskiin was checked directly because it is the strongest possible counter-example -- 390 active video ads for a filtered showerhead sold on skin and hair outcomes. It does NOT open on water quality. Every ad read opens 'eskiin will give you your best skin & hair - guaranteed', with filtration and chlorine appearing in the second sentence as mechanism.

So the brand whose entire product IS water quality still opens on outcome. That makes this unclaimed as a POSITION rather than proof the argument sells -- the opposite of the 'validated demand' reading, and a weaker claim than it first looked.
LIMIT: ~390 ads, one page read, and that page was a single repeated creative.

natural_owner_test.why: Filtered showerhead sold entirely on skin and hair outcomes. 390 active video ads. No brand has a stronger claim to 'your water is the problem'.
natural_owner_test.finding: Opens on outcome — 'eskiin will give you your best skin & hair, guaranteed' — with chlorine and filtration demoted to sentence two as mechanism.
natural_owner_test.verdict: FAILS — the position's natural owner declines it, which is evidence it does not sell rather than evidence it is available.

claimed_angles.description: GLP-1 / weight-loss facial volume loss ('Ozempic face') — rapid loss deflates the midface and is the single loudest skin conversation of the moment.

evidence: Worked hard, but by INGESTIBLES, not topical skincare: Ownist Global (collagen shot), Lemon & Co. (collagen elixir, live since 30 Oct 2025), Heart & Soil (GLP-1 stack).
No topical facial skincare advertiser found running it. Still open for a topical brand -- but the audience has already been taught the frame by supplement ads, so it is not virgin territory.

claimed_angles.description: Pregnancy- and nursing-safe actives — a hard constraint that forces a routine rebuild and makes switching brand-agnostic.

evidence: Primally Pure Skincare — topical, creator ad, pregnancy-safe switch as the hook.
Secret Saviours — topical pregnancy skincare system.
Tiny field (6 ads total vs ~33,000 mentioning menopause), so claimed but barely contested -- arguably the most attractive of the demoted angles.

claimed_angles.description: Reactive / sensitive skin as identity, not spec — 'if your face reacts to everything'. Barrier appears in the corpus only as mechanism inside body copy, never as who the viewer is.

evidence: FALSIFIED on the generous query. 'reactive skin' was too narrow and returned a misleading near-miss.

CeraVe opens on it: 'If your skin squeaks, your barrier is weak.' Beauty From Bees opens on it: 'If your skin feels tight, flaky, or itchy no matter what you use -- this is for you.' Both are the identity-lead this angle claimed nobody ran.

claimed_angles.description: Dermatologist as ally. Every derm reference in the corpus is adversarial — dismissive, hiding something, overprescribing. Nobody runs calm, genuine clinical endorsement, which is wide open precisely because everyone vacated it.

evidence: FALSIFIED on a deeper read. The earlier UNCLAIMED_POSITION verdict came from one page of a narrow query and was wrong.

Opened on directly by: Dove ('New Dove Advanced Care is the #1 dermatologist recommended brand'), SkinCeuticals ('Add the #1 Dermatologist Recommended Vitamin C Serum', 13 ads on the creative), Eucerin, CLn Skin Care, Bio-Oil. CeraVe carries it as the ad headline.

STRUCTURE WORTH KEEPING: our corpus is DTC challengers, who treat dermatologists adversarially. The legacy brands open on derm endorsement. So the position is not empty -- it is held by the incumbents a challenger defines itself against. That is a positioning divide, not an opportunity.
